Exciting News! Introducing the "The State of Our Climate" R Shiny App: Our team at the University of Washington has been hard at work on our first R Shiny App project, and we're thrilled to unveil "The State of Our Climate"! Check it out here: https://lnkd.in/gTHxM5ZE Our app focuses on the critical aspects of average temperatures and velocity of temperature change. By analyzing these factors using time series temperature data from UC Berkeley, we've gained invaluable insights that contribute to a newfound understanding of the global climate crisis. Major Takeaways: - Regional Disparities: We've aggregated average temperature patterns by cities and countries. Certain areas have experienced accelerated temperature growth, driving the climate crisis. The correlation between emissions and rising temperatures underscores the need for global collaboration. - Temporal Dynamics: Our Velocity of Temperature Change Over Time scatter plot highlights the accelerating speed of temperature shifts. Zooming into specific time frames reveals rapid temperature changes, calling for urgent policies to address this trend. - Customizable Analysis: Our Shiny app empowers users with interactive widgets to tailor their exploration. Whether it's tracking temperature trends over time or exploring each region in more depth, users can derive insights aligned with their goals, driving informed decisions for positive climate action. Many thanks to my amazing team members for their dedication and hard work: - Derek : Temperature Velocity and World Maps implementation, coauthoring app text. - Alicia : World Maps by city visualization. - Sierra : Coauthoring app text. - Myself: Repository setup, Temperature Change visualization, CSS styling, and code debugging. I invite you to join us in getting curious about climate change, uncovering insights, and advocating for systemic change. We must work together for a sustainable and resilient future. #ClimateAction #DataVisualization #ClimateInsights #Sustainability #TeamWork #UniversityOfWashington

Amazon Leo recently deployed 29 more satellites on the Leo Atlas 8 (LA-08) mission, and our summer interns experienced it from Mission Control. On July 2, ULA's Atlas V rocket carried 29 Amazon Leo satellites to low Earth orbit. It was our 14th mission, bringing our total to nearly 400, the third-largest constellation in orbit. The interns in this video were part of it. From our operations center in Redmond, Washington, they witnessed the team take control of the satellites minutes after launch from Cape Canaveral, FL. Not a bad way to spend a summer. Leo's next launch with ULA will be on their new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket, with service to customers beginning later this year.

This past Friday marked my last day with The University of Texas System Office of Technology & Information Services (OTIS) after an incredible 11 months. I'm incredibly grateful to everyone across OTIS and the UT System administration for your kindness, support, and the opportunity to learn and grow. The experiences, mentorship, and relationships I built during my time there have had a lasting impact on me, and I'll always be thankful for that chapter. Today, I'm excited to begin my career as a Cybersecurity Engineer on the Threat Exposure Management team at PayPal. I look forward to building on everything I've learned at UT System and throughout my internships at PayPal as I continue to grow both personally and professionally. Thank you, UT System, for everything. PayPal, here's to new beginnings!

After a year as a software engineer at Roblox , I will be pursuing a J.D. at New York University School of Law . Since my first internship at Roblox in 2023, working alongside such talented and collaborative colleagues has been a privilege. My work there also focused my curiosity about the law. The advertising infrastructure I built was deeply informed by changing American and international regulatory and privacy regimes: GDPR, COPPA, and direct interventions from state attorneys general. I look forward to exploring trade, administrative, and antitrust law and to gaining new interests in my three years at NYU. Thank you to everyone who supported me in my software career and to those who helped me build the path I'm on now!

Well, it officially happened. I quit my dream job to found Palace Cybersecurity. Nine years ago, my first day as an intern at Google was terrifying. I was missing an immigration document that required my immediate termination. I suppose my career could have just ended there, but Google was a kind company. We quickly sorted it out and got on with the internship. As it turned out, especially back then, Google cared about its people and doing the right thing. I learned a lot about software, research, professionalism, and doing right by people. I’m grateful to all my mentors and teammates that made Google a special place. I hope I bring that magic to Palace.
